title: Reflectional and Rotational Symmetry
seo_title: Geometry Reflectional and Rotational Symmetry Worksheets (TEKS G.3D)
standard_text: G.3D identify and distinguish between reflectional and rotational symmetry in a plane figure
meta_desc: Free Geometry symmetry worksheets for Texas TEKS G.3D: lines of symmetry, order and angle of rotational symmetry, and reflectional versus rotational symmetry. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Regular n-gon: n lines, order n, angle 360° ÷ n.
key_sub: A parallelogram has rotational symmetry only.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Reflectional (line) symmetry: a line splits the figure into two mirror images.
  • Rotational symmetry: the figure looks the same after a turn of less than 360°.
  • The order is how many times it matches itself in a full turn. The smallest angle is 360° ÷ order.
  • A regular n-gon has n lines of symmetry and order n.

Examples

Example

Regular hexagon

6 lines

360° ÷ 6

Answer: 6 lines of symmetry; rotates by 60°

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting a rectangle's diagonalsThey are not lines of symmetry.
Giving 360° as the angleEvery figure looks the same after 360°.
Thinking a parallelogram has a line of symmetryIt has only rotational symmetry.

items.q: Which transformation maps a rectangle onto itself?
c: A rotation of 180° about its center
A rotation of 90° about its center
items.e: A rectangle that is not a square only matches itself after a half turn (or a reflection over a line through the midpoints of opposite sides). A rotation of 180° about its center.

items.q: A figure is reflected over two parallel lines. Which single transformation has the same result?
items.e: Two reflections over parallel lines make a translation, twice the distance between the lines. A translation.

items.q: Which transformation is NOT a rigid transformation?
items.e: A dilation changes the size, so lengths are not preserved. A dilation with scale factor 2.

items.q: A point is rotated 360° about the origin. Where does it end up?
c: On the opposite side of the origin
items.e: A full turn brings every point back to where it started. At its starting point.

items.q: Which transformation changes the orientation of a figure (clockwise order of the vertices)?
items.e: A reflection flips a figure, so A, B, C clockwise become A′, B′, C′ counterclockwise. A reflection.

items.q: What is the smallest angle of rotation that maps a regular 12-gon onto itself?
items.e: Rotating by one vertex: 360° ÷ 12 = 30°.

items.q: Under a translation, a segment and its image are always
c: Parallel (or on the same line) and the same length
items.e: A translation slides every point the same distance in the same direction. Parallel (or on the same line) and the same length.

items.q: Triangle ABC is rotated 90° about the origin. AB = 7 and m∠B = 48°. What are A′B′ and m∠B′?
items.e: A rotation is rigid, so lengths and angles do not change. A′B′ = 7 and m∠B′ = 48°.

items.q: What is the smallest angle of rotation that maps a regular nonagon onto itself?
items.e: Rotating by one vertex: 360° ÷ 9 = 40°.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a regular pentagon have?
items.e: A regular polygon with 5 sides has 5 lines of symmetry. 5.

items.q: A figure is reflected over the y-axis and then over the x-axis. Which single transformation has the same result?
c: A rotation of 180° about the origin
A rotation of 90° about the origin
items.e: (x, y) → (−x, y) → (−x, −y), which is the 180° rotation rule. A rotation of 180° about the origin.

items.q: What is the smallest angle of rotation that maps a regular pentagon onto itself?
items.e: Rotating by one vertex: 360° ÷ 5 = 72°.

items.q: What is the smallest angle of rotation that maps a regular hexagon onto itself?

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a regular decagon have?
items.e: A regular polygon with 10 sides has 10 lines of symmetry. 10.

items.q: Which transformation does NOT map a square onto itself?
c: A rotation of 90° about its center
A rotation of 270° about its center
A reflection over a line through one vertex and the midpoint of a side
items.e: Squares have 4 lines of symmetry: 2 diagonals and 2 lines through midpoints of opposite sides. A reflection over a line through one vertex and the midpoint of a side.

items.q: Which is preserved by every rigid transformation?
items.e: Rigid motions keep size and shape, so the image is congruent. Orientation can change in a reflection. Side lengths and angle measures.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a parallelogram (not a rectangle or rhombus) have?
items.e: No line folds it onto itself, although it has 180° rotational symmetry. 0.

items.q: What is the smallest angle of rotation that maps a regular octagon onto itself?
items.e: Rotating by one vertex: 360° ÷ 8 = 45°.

items.q: If a rigid transformation maps triangle ABC to triangle DEF, what can you conclude?
c: The triangles are similar but not congruent
Point A and point D are the same point
The triangles have the same orientation
items.e: Rigid transformations preserve distance and angle measure, so the figures are congruent. The triangles are congruent.

items.q: What is the smallest angle of rotation that maps a regular decagon onto itself?
items.e: Rotating by one vertex: 360° ÷ 10 = 36°.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a isosceles triangle (not equilateral) have?
items.e: Only the line through the vertex angle and the midpoint of the base. 1.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a regular nonagon have?
items.e: A regular polygon with 9 sides has 9 lines of symmetry. 9.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a regular hexagon have?
items.e: A regular polygon with 6 sides has 6 lines of symmetry. 6.
